Otherwise that person must have come directly from a superior command and then they could enter without our knowledge or permission, but in such circumstances they have to undertake all the risk and all the responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: As far as I can interpret the rules of service of the armed forces and regarding what we've mentioned concerning the local commands, any officer in the territory temporarily has to abide by the decisions of the local commander. This is clearly stated. And the local commander is obliged to inform him of the decisions in place in the area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The person entering the AOR has to report that. He cannot enter without approval and without our knowledge. That's the regulation. Therefore, the person who headed the column or the team should have stopped by and to let us know. Perhaps to tell me: Listen, we're going in, regarding this and that. You've got nothing to do with it, but we just wanted to let you know, so that there would be no friendly fire or any such thing. And then the risk is all theirs.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: And when the local commander -- just a second, I want to finish my question. When the local commander encounters an officer temporarily within his location, he needs to warn him of the decisions in place put there by the local commander in keeping with his powers?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to explain that. The person who came in should have stopped by.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. The officer you were mentioning, did you specify the rules and decisions you put in place within your area of responsibility as the local commander, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He had his own assignment, and he was about to carry it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: As the local commander, were you duty-bound to inform him of that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't the local commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that by written orders you were appointed local commander, but as you are now stating, you ceased to be that by some oral order?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't the local commander. If we are talking about the area, I have just explained. It was defined, but then it -- another appointment was made. As regards the officers there, I could no longer control that part of the area, and I had no right to.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: That's precisely what I asked you. By a written order you were appointed local commander for Ovcara, Jakubovac, and Grabovo. You are now claiming that by a decision of an officer you ceased to be the Ovcara local commander. Is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I wasn't appointed local commander. Rather, it was the person who was there with the agreement of the superior command. The superior command -- or rather, an organ from the superior command, came there and installed that person. He was there at Ovcara. He wasn't, at the time, under my command.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vojnovic, so as not to go back to Exhibit 418, we've already gone through it in detail today, but it clearly states there that you were the local commander for Ovcara, Grabovo, Jakubovac, once the 20th Partisan Brigade had withdrawn commanded by Lieutenant Misovic, but not the area of responsibility. Mr. Vojnovic, I won't go back to the orders by which you, as the local commander of the three localities subdivided the area appointing various commanders, one for Ovcara and the other one for Grabovo and Jakubovac. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it isn't so.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Please explain.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted) was not one of my officers at the time. Vukasinovic was not my officer who was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vojnovic, did you sign the order appointing the aforementioned gentleman, the local commander of Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the agreement of the operations group command.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: That's not what one can read in the order. I'm asking you whether you've signed it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But, as I said, with the consent of.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: I told you that you had some subordinated units in the sector that had several hundred men and armoured vehicles. I believe you were able to use those units in order to establish order and security for the prisoners in the hangar, even when the officer whose name we don't want to mention who was the local commander came to see you to warn you of the withdrawal of your military policemen. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: On that occasion the aforementioned local commander, did he tell you that the situation at the hangar was calm, that order had been established, and that the prisoners were safe?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact details of what he said, but there was order. Whether they were safe and what could potentially take place, that was not something we could foresee.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Would you be so kind as to pick up one of the statements before you, in particular the one given to the investigative judge of the district court in Novi Sad on the 21st of November, 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For my learned friends, this is page 5 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: For you, Mr. Vojnovic, that's page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Your statement given to the investigative judge, Mr. Alimpic, in Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Page 4 of that statement.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me when you've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Passage number 3, and it starts, "What (redacted) says is accurate."

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: "That arrived at the command at my command in Negoslavci at around 2200 hours and asked for the command to be relocated. He had previously told me that Captain Vezmarovic had told him that order had been re-established in the hangar and that the prisoners were safe and that Captain Karanfilov, a security officer with Operations Group South, had told him to pull his soldiers out and that the Territorial Defence unit would now assume control over the prisoners." Did you state that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: And as far as you remember, you were told this on the evening of the 20th, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So what was I to do now? What you just suggested, summon units for security, that sort of thing? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have Exhibit 422 placed on our screens? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vojnovic, this is an order of the OG South command dated the 21st of November, 1991, 464-1, signed by Chief of Staff Miodrag Panic. In item 4 of this order the units of the Vukovar TO are resubordinated to your 80th Motorised Brigade, the focus being to guard and supervise the area taken and its most sensitive features. Did you receive this order on the 21st of November?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if it reached us. It may have reached us. If indeed it did, I must have been aware of it, but this is the 21st, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was produced at 6.00 in the morning on the 21st. Do you remember seeing that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. We never received documents in the morning, usually later on in the day. This was produced at 6.00 in the morning, well, then...

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 21st of November, 1991, you were still the local commander at Grabovo, Ovcara, and Jakubovac. And after your unit took over from OG South, you became the commander of Vukovar as well, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: On the 21st of November, as local commander, were you not supposed to secure the area, the crime scene at Ovcara, that was within your area of responsibility, to secure the site until the military investigators arrived?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody told me to do that. I wasn't given an assignment like that, nor did I know about the TO members, who they were, who they were subordinated to. I know I received an oral order from the commander to line up the volunteers, to surrender and hand back their weapons, but that was never done. We did secure the hospital, and the SUP building later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After this was over, just to be clear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: As the military investigators, and I suppose civilian investigators too, were in Vukovar at a time when you were still local commander there, did you ever tell them about this, about the information you had concerning this?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an evening meeting with the commander of OG South. I'm not sure when this was, it might have been on the 21st. He said that investigators would be there.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, on the 22nd.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: But what I want to know is: When did they come? Was it late in November? Late in December?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, several days after this happened he said that the investigators would arrive on the 20 something of November, 25th, perhaps, perhaps not, and that the right conditions should be secured for their work. I did not see any investigators there myself. I did see some. I know Colonel Papic was there, he was the prosecutor at the time, I suppose, with the military court or something. But I didn't know the rest of them. They were in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps know investigating magistrate, Miodrag Salic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Come again?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Miodrag Salic, investigating magistrate of the military court?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know. Not familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: All right. On the 21st of November, Mr. Vojnovic, you said you had held a meeting with your subordinate officers at which you cautioned them about the fact that what had occurred at Ovcara should never happen again?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And that they should tell everybody that such things must never occur again; that they should prevent acts of retaliation, especially with people of different ethnicities involved; that orders should be complied with, and that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: You said the commander told you that there should be no acts of retaliation; that's not in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that every and any act of retaliation must be prevented or foiled.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: At one point in time you took over the powers of OG South in the area -- actually, you did this when you moved with your command post and the staff units to the barracks in Vukovar, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I assumed the powers of OG South after OG South had left for Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We could please have document 0D00-0539 on our screens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just say this too: Throughout my long military career, I never noticed a document being produced at 6.00 in the morning; that is unheard of, in my experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vojnovic, this is your order dated the 22nd of November, 1991, strictly confidential 37-3?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: This is about the transfer of units to the Vukovar barracks, to the brigade command, on the 22nd of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So it was after this order that you moved with your command and the units to the Vukovar barracks, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek that this be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: It will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 444, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could please have 425, Exhibit 425 on our screens. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have got no copies of that particular document, we have just checked. I don't know whether there's been some error, but I've check with my case manager as well. Would my learned friend happen to have a hard copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which document is my learned friend talking about? I'll try to do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: It is the document that became the transfer of units to Vukovar on the 22nd -- to the Vukovar barracks on the 22nd of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All folders should be identical. It is certainly not deliberate if that document is not in your folder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Mr. Moore, it seems to be under tab 11 in the folder we have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there is any problem, I will make sure to have a copy made for my learned friend following this session.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vojnovic, this is a regular combat report, OG South command, 473-1, strictly confidential, 22nd of November, 1991, 1800 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could please zoom in on the last two paragraphs of this document, and if we could just pull the document up a little. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vojnovic, you see the second last passage there. It says, "During the day all the measures were taken for the 80th Motorised Brigade" --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it -- yeah, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: So, let me try this again. "During the day all the measures were taken for the 80th Motorised Brigade to assume all the organisational and command functions in the area of responsibility of OG South." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies to the interpreters. I sped up a little and I lost track right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: I'll try to do this again. "During the day all the necessary measures were taken for the 80th Motorised Brigade to assume the organisational and command functions in the area of responsibility of OG South." The next passage reads: "The command of the 80th Motorised Brigade has received all the instructions and documents needed to set up command and control in the area of responsibility of OG South." Is this accurate, Mr. Vojnovic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: After you got the control and command -- the command and control documents, is it not a fact that you assumed the responsibilities of OG South? This is the last tact of a hand-over between two units, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the 22nd of November, everything was over. There was certain equipment to be exchanged, certain plans, communications, equipment -- yes, this strikes me as perfectly all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Vojnovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have another document here. This is 0D00-0569. Can that be shown, please? We have a copy of the document for my learned friend. I see that this is a problem, so we can provide it. We will need to go into private session for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my learned friend can perhaps deal with this in the re-examination, but I thought that yesterday during the examination-in-chief he thought that these were possibly crimes and that, as a result of that, there was this remark that investigative organs would come to investigate the possible atrocities in the area of Vukovar. But if the Trial Chamber deems it necessary, I can put a question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Mr. Moore, can you take this up in re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: In my submission, it's a matter for the Defence to put their case to the witness. Clearly an ability or an order to commence investigations is an element that has to be considered by the Court. It may well be part of the defendant's case or may not. And in my submission, the Rules are quite clear that the important elements of a defendant's case should be put to the witness specifically so he has a chance to reply one way or other and cannot be dealt by way of re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vojnovic, as part of the asanacija or cleansing of terrain operations in relation to the victims, did your unit, in accordance with the command of the 1st Military District and OG South, instructed to provide the military forensic experts, crime technicians, investigators and other experts who were in the Vukovar area in the period that you mentioned here - and they were headed by Colonel Basic - and was your unit supposed to provide services for them?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said that at a meeting on the 21st or on the 22nd, the commander said: The investigative organs are coming tomorrow. I don't know how many exactly, 30 or 40 of them. They need to be billeted and be provided with work space. I personally know that a part or a small number of my soldiers were helping the -- the present minister of defence, Zoran Stankovic, who was investigating the corpses at the Ciglana. I know that some of them were also assisting Colonel Basic in moving the corpses, dead bodies of humans and livestock. It's possible that there was some other -- there were some assistance being provided, but this is all I know about.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: I'm going to tell you about my client's thesis, that on the 21st --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said it was either the 21st or the 22nd.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: If you're talking about the meeting of the 21st, the regular briefing in the afternoon, my client was not in Negoslavci, so perhaps you could have talked with the Chief of Staff, Miodrag Panic, possibly. If we're talking about the 22nd in the afternoon, then Mr. Mrksic was at the regular briefing.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not what Panic said. This was what Colonel Mrksic said, and it was at the regular briefing.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that there is an order on this from the 1st Military District and the OG South group on the cleansing of the terrain?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm -- assume that such an order exists, if I received it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one mistake in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: It's page 107, line 23, I think you said that Lieutenant -- Colonel Mrksic told you that on the 22nd in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said it was either on the 21st or the 22nd, and since you said that he wasn't there on the 21st, then it must have been on the 22nd.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'm being warned about my microphone. Now we're going to look at a 65 ter document on the screen, that is document 103, and it's ERN number 0327-2263. The English version has the same number. Thank you very much. Can we zoom in on the document a little bit?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Can you see it, Mr. Vojnovic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is an order regulating the clearing of the terrain, it's the command of the 1st Military District, confidential number 8-180/31, dated 16th of November, 1991. Here it is assigned to the Guards Motorised Brigade, which is crossed out, and it says "80th Motorised Brigade." He says --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why it was crossed out. I cooperated directly with the command of the 1st Military District. It states in item 1, to whom the document is addressed to.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you: Did you get this document from OG South command?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really don't know. There were so many orders, but I know that we did work to remove the corpses, waste material, carcasses, de-mining.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: You don't remember?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall, but we did work on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this order as an exhibit, if there are no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: It will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 445, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, and now I would like to complete my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Vasic. Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, I am Borivoje Borovic, and I represent Miroslav Radic. First question: We heard from one of your officers who testified here that one of your battalions was in the area of Petrova Gora. Did you hear of that, and which was -- which period was this?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that it was in the Petrova Gora sector. One of our battalions was in the beginning when we came at the very entrance to Vukovar. I don't know all the parts. I know of Petrova Gora, but I don't know if it was there specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Dragi Vukosavljevic, who testified here, was certain that your 3rd Battalion was located in the Petrova Gora sector, that he visited it, that it had its own security line at Petrova Gora, and that that battalion had about 400 men. Would you accept as -- this as being correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the first part of the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know the exact sector we're talking about; it could have been at the entrance to Vukovar or to the left side or to the right side.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. The interpreters didn't hear the first part of answer, so we will go again. So number one: Is it true what Dragi Vukosavljevic said, that one of your battalions was in the area of Petrova Gora and that he visited that battalion there on a number of occasions?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that if Dragi said that, then I can agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Second question: Do you know which period this could have been in, which month?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it was, is that right? I think it could have been in November or December.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who was the commander of the battalion?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The battalion was under the command of Captain First Class -- I think his name was Lalovic. I can't recall his first name.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Did you not confirm earlier that that battalion numbered about 400 men, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the response to the call-up was weak. It didn't number 400, somewhat fewer men, somewhere in the range of 300 to 350 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What did I hear, 300 to --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 300 to 400. I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, very well. Thank you. Did that battalion take part in combat operations along the axis where it was located?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did not participate directly in the operations. I don't know exactly to whom it was resubordinated exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Was it resubordinated at all, or was it in coordinated action with other units?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in coordinated action with other units.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday I followed your answer on the topic of the participation of your units in the wartime events in Vukovar. Can we conclude then that this battalion was a reserve battalion, and when it was used it mostly was in defensive operations?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think all of our units --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about this unit.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There -- every unit that was for itself was in defensive actions mostly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: That means that that also includes the 3rd Battalion that was in the Petrova Gora region?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that the OG South commander sent the 3rd Battalion to the area of responsibility of the 1st Assault Detachment in order to go into coordinated action to secure the front lines? Can we agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm not sure where that was exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at Exhibit 156 on the monitors, please? Would you please be so kind and try to zoom in on the middle portion of the picture by a factor of two, if possible, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you see this on your screen, Mr. Vojnovic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. I'm not sure what I'm supposed to be looking at.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind, take that pen there and try to mark with a number 1 the area of deployment of your 3rd Battalion, the first time around?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't -- or rather, at the very entry to Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Number 1, please.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, is this the railroad track? I know that it was at the very entry to Vukovar, there was a pub right there, and it was right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you please circle that number 1?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now do the next area where your 3rd Battalion was, can you mark that with a number 2?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you spot Petrova Gora on this map or the neighbourhood known as Leva Supoderica, do you know that? Can you show that to us?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about Suporderica, I know about Petrova Gora, but I can't see either on that map. I can't mark them for you with any degree of certainty or precision.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The neighbourhood known as Leva Supoderica or the 6th Proletarian Division and the neighbourhood known as Hollywood, you know about those but you can't mark them for us, can you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've been to Hollywood, I remember that, but I can't see it on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Then my question is: You've heard me mention all these different areas. What about your battalion, the 3rd Battalion, did they take any steps in any of those areas ever, Leva Supoderica, the 6th Proletarian Division, or Hollywood, which is on Ivana Gorana Kovacica Street?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was there in that neighbourhood, like you have -- as you have suggested.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. There is no need to draw that or to mark anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe the witness has described the area where his 3rd Battalion was, so I think that's sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: My question: Do you know how the 3rd Battalion in Kragujevac was set up, people were mobilised from which companies exactly?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 3rd Battalion was not from Kragujevac to begin with; it was either from Raca or Topola.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Was it maybe set up by mobilising people from the red flag, Crvena Zastava, car factory?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was the 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you go to all these areas where your battalion was and your unit?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did go to see Captain Lalovic. I toured all of my units.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. While touring all these areas, did you ever come across Captain Radic? If so -- but you didn't?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I didn't know Captain Radic, and I didn't see him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Next question: Given that you didn't see him, if I tell you that the 3rd Battalion, your battalion, was occupying positions along an axis also taken by the 3rd company of the 1st Assault Detachment, you who had the rank of lieutenant colonel at the time, do you believe that the 3rd Battalion of the 80th Motorised Brigade was under the command of Captain Radic, who was a company commander, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Whose orders did its work and the use of their units depend on?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean Captain Radic?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This depended on my orders, for as long as they were under my command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can a battalion commander assess a unit that has just been resubordinated to him, or can he prefer this unit over the entire composition as a company commander?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't get that one, sorry. Can you repeat that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can he resubordinate a unit that had just been resubordinated to him, its entire composition, to his company commander or not?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not clear about that question. Can a battalion commander --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- resubordinate --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: -- a unit that has been resubordinated to him --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- resubordinated to somebody else --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: -- to his own company commander?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From his own unit, from the composition of his own battalion, you mean? The company commander cannot -- I mean -- well, the battalion commander -- I don't know. What is this about now? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. A specific question: The decision to carry out combat activities, what does that mean to a battalion commander? An order by a commander of one of his superior units, can he change that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order of a superior commander can only be changed with previous approval from whoever had ordered that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does that not mean that this decision is the most important order at this point in time, and there is no way he can change it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not without appropriate approval. If there is something that needs changing, he can make a couple of changes but he must inform others about any changes that he has made. A certain amount of initiative is approved in certain situations, but this needs to be reported.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have Exhibit 401 on our screens now; this is the war log of the Guards Motorised Brigade. The entry is dated 15th of November, 1991, 1800 hours. The page reference is 43. The English is 38. Same log. Page 43. The 15th of November, 1800 hours. Could you please zoom in a little.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vojnovic, this entry here says that the OG South commander carried out -- or amended his previous decision of the 14th of November, 1991, as follows. The first bullet says - excuse me, just don't interrupt me. I'll read slowly - that: "The TO detachment of Stara Pazova is hereby resubordinated to the 3rd Battalion of the 80th Motorised Brigade." Next: "The 3rd Battalion of the 80th Motorised Brigade," so the same battalion, "shall leave JOD-1," the assault detachment 1, "and be placed under the command of the 80th Motorised Brigade." And the last thing we have is that: "The 80th Motorised Brigade in future operations should cease control of the area of the 6th Proletarian Division neighbourhood, Leva and the Desna Supoderica and the area along the River Vuka." Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that on the 15th of November, 1991, you received oral amendments to this assignment by Colonel Mrksic to do with the future deployment of your units? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this battalion?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Elements of your units in general.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But you do allow for the possibility, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I leave the possibility open.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, based on this entry that we have just looked at, that the 3rd Battalion of the 80th Motorised Brigade left the composition of the 1st Assault Detachment and that, at least up until that date, it had been involved along the axis of operations of the 1st Assault Detachment, commanded by Major Borivoje Tesic. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure who the commander was of that detachment, I don't know about the dates and everything that you're suggest. I know that Tesic was some commander there, the commander of a detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can we please agree -- I've covered this ground slowly and gradually because we're talking about the 1st JOD, the 1st Assault Detachment, and your own 3rd Battalion. Captain Radic could not possibly have been command of your own 3rd Battalion, it could only have been the battalion commander, Major Tesic, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Finally, can we conclude that your own 3rd Battalion of the 80th Motorised Brigade could, by no means, have been incorporated into the 3rd Company under the command of Captain Radic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: My next question: Do you know who and when appointed Miroljub Vujovic commander of Vukovar's TO defence? If you do, based on which other document was that done?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that before our departure the commander of OG South said something about an order arriving, I think. I know that Miroljub Vujovic was appointed commander of Vukovar's TO; his deputy was Stanko Vujanovic. The commander for the rear units was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get the name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- Darko Fot was in charge of another section and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean, based on your own military expertise, that he could not have been appointed commander of the Vukovar TO by a company commander, and certainly not the commander of the 3rd Company of the Guards Motorised Brigade, Miroslav Radic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no way. First I hear of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So he didn't appoint him, we do know that for a fact, but I want your expertise. There are a number of documents that we've looked at during this trial referring to Vujovic as commander of the Petrova Gora TO detachment. Do you know who appointed him to that position?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the name was of that unit, whether it was a detachment or a company, but I did hear that he was the person in charge over at over at Petrova Gora.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What if I told you that this was a detachment; in terms of the establishment, how many people would that mean?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all detachments are the same size, but I would say between 350 and 400. It's just a little smaller than an infantry battalion normally is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that he could have certainly been appointed to that position by the commander of the 3rd Company, Captain Radic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it means [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I see that it is time to stop. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: I see that there is an error in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: There should be -- the -- too many mics going on at the same time, I believe. I understood the last answer to be a negative.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that is clearly a negative, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: May I deal with certain housekeeping matters? I don't know how long my learned friends will be tomorrow. I will not be dealing with the next witness. If there is any way they could indicate how long they may be in cross-examination, then that would assist the Prosecution for trying to work out the timetable. I don't know if my learned friends -- I know Mr. Lukic is always succinct and very brief, to the point, but if there's any way that Mr. Borovic and Mr. Lukic could assist us, we would be very grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are trying to do the best we can for the OTP; on the other hand, I don't believe we have ever been given advance notice of their examination-in-chief in terms of how long it will take. I do believe that a single session will do for the rest of my cross-examination tomorrow, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to say something different from Mr. Borovic. When we ask for the duration of Mr. Moore's examination-in-chief, he's usually quite evasive. He said five hours in relation to one particular witness and it was one and a half hours. As for my cross-examination, I can't promise anything definitive, but I think I might take up to two sessions. That is the best I can do at this point, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. I was looking at the estimate for the whole of this testimony, which was four hours to start with. We've gone much beyond it, but I am confident that counsel will be succinct tomorrow and that we will respect those time-schedules. So we are going to rise for today and we will resume tomorrow morning at 9.30. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
